## Research Vision

Climate change is transforming ocean ecosystems, fisheries, food systems, and coastal societies. My research develops interdisciplinary evidence, models, and future scenarios to understand these changes and support sustainable, equitable, and resilient ocean futures.

## Research Themes

::: {.research-grid}

::: {.research-card}
### Climate Change and Marine Ecosystems

Understanding how warming, marine extremes, ocean acidification, deoxygenation, and circulation changes affect marine biodiversity and ecosystem functioning.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Blue Food Futures

Assessing the future of fisheries and aquatic food systems and identifying pathways that support food security, sustainability, and equity.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Biodiversity and Ocean Sustainability

Connecting ecological change with conservation, governance, and sustainable development from local to global scales.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Scenarios and Ocean Futures

Developing models, scenarios, and storylines to explore risks, adaptation, tipping points, and alternative pathways for ocean futures.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Science–Policy Leadership

Contributing scientific evidence and assessment leadership through international processes including the IPCC and IPBES.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Training and Knowledge Mobilization

Supporting the next generation of ocean researchers and connecting scientific knowledge with policy, practice, and public understanding.
:::

:::

## Changing Ocean Research Unit

I lead the [Changing Ocean Research Unit](https://coru.oceans.ubc.ca), an interdisciplinary research group at the University of British Columbia.

[Visit the CORU website](https://coru.oceans.ubc.ca){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
